summary: This article explains space weather and solar storms (flares, CMEs, SEPs) and how they affect Earth, including geomagnetic storms, power grid risks from GICs, and satellite disruptions. It cites recent events from September 2023 to February 2024 and quotes experts on the risks and forecasting. It also outlines engineering countermeasures such as radiation hardening, safe mode protocols, resistant transformers, and improved forecasting.
one_line: Overview of solar storms, their effects on power grids and satellites, and the engineering and forecasting measures used to mitigate them.
key_facts: Space weather refers to conditions on the Sun and in the solar wind, magnetosphere, ionosphere, and thermosphere that can affect spaceborne and ground-based technology.
Solar storms can launch billions of tons of plasma into space at speeds of up to a million miles an hour.
Solar flares are intense bursts of radiation from the release of magnetic energy associated with sunspots, and X-class flares are the most intense.
Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) directed towards Earth can take between one to three days to arrive, depending on their speed.
On September 8, 2023, a powerful X-class solar flare followed by a significant CME was observed by the Solar Dynamics Observatory.
By September 11, 2023, satellite communications experienced intermittent disruptions, raising concern among GPS-based system operators and users.
On October 30, 2023, Dr. Emily Petrov of the National Grid warned that geomagnetically induced currents can cause widespread blackouts and damage expensive transformers.
Geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) flowing through power lines cause voltage instability and transformer damage.
In extreme cases, solar storms can cause satellites to deorbit prematurely.
Satellite protective measures include shielding, redundant systems, and placing satellites in 'safe mode' where sensitive parts are turned off.
On December 1, 2023, Dr. David Gomez compared predicting solar storms to predicting weather on Earth, a complex, dynamic system.
On February 16, 2024, a new satellite designed by engineer Rachel Aniston and her team launched with radiation-hardened chips capable of withstanding intense solar activity.
Grid protections include space weather forecast monitoring, grid-stabilizing technology, and development of transformers less susceptible to overheating from GICs.
